correctness.rationale: For distributional real BV, the signed step representation and convexity on individual averaging cells yield the exact finite-grid supremum. Strict binomial stochastic monotonicity gives one crossing for each response. The cell matrix is explicitly rational bistochastic with simple positive polynomial eigenvalues. Reflection-odd restriction has strictly positive entries, so Perron–Frobenius forces the strictly signed left second eigenvector; spectral projection and ∫|x-1/2|=1/4 then give the rational coefficient and eventual centrality. All quantifiers and n=1 exceptional case are handled. Standalone checker reproduces rational matrix/left eigenvalues and numerical norms for degrees through eight; finite checks do not stand in for the proof.

originality.rationale: The new claim is the exact all-power norm of the classical Kantorovich iterates from the invariant mean on real distributional BV, plus rational leading asymptotic coefficient and eventual centrally located sharp single jumps. Cooper–Waldron gives the eigenvalues, not this norm; Kivinukk–Metsmägi controls variation of the identity defect for smooth functions; the generalized-operator convergence paper treats a different map and qualitative convergence. The tested published records and recoverable prior claims do not directly state or dominate the present combination. Priority remains tentative owing to unindexed sources.
residual_risks: An unindexed source could already present the particular sharp invariant-mean BV norm, possibly expressed as a finite stochastic-matrix or operator-ergodicity formula.
The finite-r maximization has not been reduced analytically to the central grid step for every r, and no such universality is claimed.
The rational leading constants are computed from existing known spectral eigenvalues, so their novelty rests on the sharp norm-and-extremizer analysis rather than the spectrum itself.

value.rationale: The invariant Lebesgue mean is the natural long-run limit of classical Kantorovich smoothing. Sharp BV-to-L1 convergence constants measure worst discontinuity-sensitive mean mixing at each finite degree and iteration, which a spectral gap alone cannot quantify. Exact finite-grid reduction, a rational optimal exponential prefactor, and eventual central step localization provide a reproducible stopping-error benchmark and describe the worst discontinuities. This is a motivated global finite-degree invariant, not an arbitrary special-case computation.
